violations.detail: .github/workflows/pages.yml is a governance file; a job may change it only when the accepted reading lists it as a deliverable and names it in an acceptance criterion

producer_report.summary: Added `cargo run -p xtask -- site`, which renders one self-contained HTML page on how firstmate handles work from `studies/firstmate-work-handling` into the gitignored `site/index.html`. The page has a viewport meta tag, responsive CSS and prefers-color-scheme dark mode. Every statement goes through one function that refuses an empty claim-id list or an id not in `claims.json`. Findings cite the claims of the transitions they name. The page shows the pinned commit (linked), HTML-escapes all study text, and ends with each claim's sources and quotes. A new `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds the page and deploys it with the official Pages actions: `contents: read` by default, and `pages: write` and `id-token: write` only on the deploy job. `ci.yml`, `athena.toml`, Cargo lints and the toolchain file are untouched. I also added the design note `docs/design/explainer-site.md`, a CHANGELOG entry, a README section and an updated D2-1 row in the requirements map. The owner must set Pages source to GitHub Actions; the live URL is unconfirmed until the first deploy.

checks_run.note: Exited 0 and wrote site/index.html. I did not run `git status` after that run to confirm the output is ignored. `git status --short` run later in the session showed only intended source edits, with no `site/` entry.
Ran to apply formatting, not as `--check`. I did not run `cargo fmt --all --check` afterwards, so the check form is unconfirmed.
First run had 6 write_with_newline errors, which I fixed with writeln!. The re-run is clean.
Full run exited 0. I could not read its saved output, so I confirmed the xtask results separately: `cargo test --locked -p xtask` shows 11 unit tests and 10 policy tests passing.

open_issues: Owner action: set the repository's Pages source to GitHub Actions in repository settings. The README names https://doodla.github.io/athena/, inferred from Cargo.toml's repository field; confirm it after the first deploy.
The Pages actions are referenced by major version tag (@v5, @v3, @v4), not pinned by commit SHA as ci.yml does for checkout, because I could not look up the SHAs. This is noted in the design note.
pages.yml has not been run on GitHub; only its text is checked, by the policy test.
pages.yml skips ./setup.sh and relies on rust-toolchain.toml and the runner's rustup. This is untested on a real runner.
mistakes: The first draft used write! with trailing newlines, which failed clippy; fixed.
I did not run `cargo fmt --all --check` after the final `cargo fmt --all`.
learnings: serde_json is already an xtask dependency, so xtask/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock needed no change.
The workspace has clippy::write_with_newline in effect; use writeln! for lines ending in a newline.
YAML is not counted as code by the M20 non-Rust check, so pages.yml needs no allow-list entry.
A test compares the strategy-view coverage table with the requirements map. I kept D2-1 as 'Not covered: ...' so the counts do not move.
The producer's Grep and Read tools cannot open files outside the working directory, including saved tool-output files.
desires: The commit SHAs of actions/configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages, to pin them like checkout in ci.yml.
The final GitHub Pages owner and URL, which I inferred from Cargo.toml's repository field.
